brief:
University of North Carolina administrators at Chapel Hill have threatened to punish and dismiss faculty members and graduate teaching assistants who refused to submit final grades for students, Shehab Wire reported. The sanctions would target instructors who declared their intent to withhold grades in support of a broader movement.

The threat emerged after faculty and teaching assistants announced they would refuse to grade student work. University officials did not publicly detail the specific companies or investments that prompted the grade-withholding action or clarify the broader movement's aims.
